item.title: I do not see any other single factor, bhikkhus, that leads to such great benefit as a mind that is tamed, guarded, restrained, and protected.…
item.description:
I do not see any other single factor, bhikkhus, that leads to such great benefit as a mind that is tamed, guarded, restrained, and protected. A tamed, guarded, restrained, and protected mind, bhikkhus, leads to great benefit.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.40

item.title: Thus, bhikkhus, disenchantment and dispassion have the knowledge and vision of liberation as their purpose, the knowledge and vision of liberation as their benefit; true…
item.description:
Thus, bhikkhus, disenchantment and dispassion have the knowledge and vision of liberation as their purpose, the knowledge and vision of liberation as their benefit; true knowledge and vision have disenchantment and dispassion as their purpose, disenchantment and dispassion as their benefit; concentration has true knowledge and vision as its purpose, true knowledge and vision as its benefit; happiness has concentration as its purpose, concentration as its benefit; tranquility has happiness as its purpose, happiness as its benefit; rapture has tranquility as its purpose, tranquility as its benefit; joy has rapture as its purpose, rapture as its benefit; non-regret has joy as its purpose, joy as its benefit; good virtues have non-regret as their purpose, non-regret as their benefit. Thus, bhikkhus, (these) conditions lead to (other) conditions; conditions complete (other) conditions, leading from the near shore to the far shore.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.2

item.title: Bhikkhus, as long as I did not directly know as it really is the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, the escape as escape,…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, as long as I did not directly know as it really is the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, the escape as escape, then, bhikkhus, I did not claim to have awakened to the unsurpassed Perfect Enlightenment in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. But when I directly knew as it really is the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, the escape as escape, then, bhikkhus, I claimed to have awakened to the unsurpassed Perfect Enlightenment... And knowledge and vision arose in me: 'Unshakable is my liberation of mind. This is my last birth. Now there is no more renewed existence.'

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.104

item.title: 'Venerable Sir, there are over a hundred and fifty training rules that I have to recite every half month. Venerable Sir, I cannot learn them.'…
item.description:
'Venerable Sir, there are over a hundred and fifty training rules that I have to recite every half month. Venerable Sir, I cannot learn them.' - 'Bhikkhu, can you learn the three trainings: the higher virtue training, the higher mind training, the higher wisdom training?' - 'Venerable Sir, I can learn the three trainings: the higher virtue training, the higher mind training, the higher wisdom training.' - 'Therefore, bhikkhu, you should train in the three trainings: the higher virtue training, the higher mind training, the higher wisdom training. If you train in the higher virtue training, the higher mind training, the higher wisdom training, then, bhikkhu, through training in these three trainings, greed will be abandoned, hatred will be abandoned, delusion will be abandoned. Through abandoning greed, abandoning hatred, abandoning delusion, you will not do what is unwholesome, you will not follow what is evil.' That bhikkhu, after some time, trained in the higher virtue training, the higher mind training, the higher wisdom training. Through training in them, greed was abandoned, hatred was abandoned, delusion was abandoned. Through abandoning greed, abandoning hatred, abandoning delusion, he did not do what was unwholesome, he did not follow what was evil.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.84

item.title: - Whatever is suffering, Rādha, therein you should abandon desire. And what, Rādha, is suffering? The eye, Rādha, is suffering; therein you should abandon desire.…
item.description:
- Whatever is suffering, Rādha, therein you should abandon desire. And what, Rādha, is suffering? The eye, Rādha, is suffering; therein you should abandon desire. Forms ... Eye-consciousness ... Eye-contact ... Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact ... that feeling is suffering; therein you should abandon desire. ... The ear ... The nose ... The tongue ... The body ... The mind is suffering; therein you should abandon desire. Mind-objects ... Mind-consciousness ... Mind-contact ... Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact ... that feeling is suffering; therein you should abandon desire. Whatever is suffering, Rādha, therein you should abandon desire.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.77

item.title: Elder Vijitasena: I will restrain you like a door restrains an elephant. I will not urge you, O mind, toward evil. You are the net…
item.description:
Elder Vijitasena:

I will restrain you like a door restrains an elephant.
I will not urge you, O mind, toward evil.
You are the net of sensual desire, you are born from the body.

Restraining you, not going, like an elephant without an open door,
O mind, you sorcerer, though you try again and again,
You will no longer wander, delighting in doing evil.

Like one holding a hook, constantly restraining an untrained elephant,
Like one using force to reform the unwilling —
So toward you, I will reform you.

Like a perfect wheel, like a well-trained horse,
So I will tame you, relying on the five powers.

I will tie you tightly with firm mindfulness.
Having tamed myself, I will tame you.
Through the weight of energy, I will pressure you.
Therefore, O mind, you will not stray from me.

From: Theragāthā 5.9

item.title: Fear, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Suffering, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Illness, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. A…
item.description:
Fear, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Suffering, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Illness, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. A boil, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. A dart, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Bondage, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. Mud, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures. The womb, bhikkhus, is a designation for sensual pleasures.
How, bhikkhus, is fear a designation for sensual pleasures? Because those who are infatuated by sensual desire, bound by sensual lust, are not freed from fear in the present life, not freed from fear in the future; therefore, fear is a designation for sensual pleasures.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.56

item.title: Bhikkhus, there are these eight bases for giving. What eight? One gives out of desire; one gives out of hatred; one gives out of delusion;…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, there are these eight bases for giving. What eight? One gives out of desire; one gives out of hatred; one gives out of delusion; one gives out of fear; one gives thinking: 'Earlier our ancestors gave, they did this before. It is not proper for me to let this ancient tradition be neglected'; one gives thinking: 'Having given this gift, after death, with the breakup of the body, I will be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world'; one gives thinking: 'When I give this gift, my mind becomes serene, and joy and happiness arise'; one gives for the adornment of the mind, for the equipment of the mind. Bhikkhus, these are the eight bases for giving.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.33

item.title: Elder Nun Bhaddā: I am the heir of the Buddha, Kassapa, well-concentrated. I know my past lives, See heavenly and hellish realms. The seer who…
item.description:
Elder Nun Bhaddā:

I am the heir of the Buddha,
Kassapa, well-concentrated.
I know my past lives,
See heavenly and hellish realms.

The seer who has destroyed birth,
Perfect in direct knowledge,
Along with these three knowledges,
Is a brahmin with three knowledges.

So too, you, Bhaddā Kapilānī,
You are one with three knowledges,
You have destroyed death,
Bearing your final body,
Having conquered Māra's army.

Seeing the danger in the world,
We both went forth.
We are tamed, our taints destroyed,
We are cooled, at peace, liberated.

From: Therīgāthā 4.1

item.title: - Bhikkhus, there are these ten grounds for resentment. What ten? Resentment is formed thinking: 'He has harmed me.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He is…
item.description:
- Bhikkhus, there are these ten grounds for resentment. What ten? Resentment is formed thinking: 'He has harmed me.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He is harming me.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He will harm me.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He has harmed someone I love, someone I like...' 'He is harming someone I love, someone I like...' 'He will harm someone I love, someone I like.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He has benefited someone I do not love, someone I do not like.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He is benefiting someone I do not love, someone I do not like.' Resentment is formed thinking: 'He will benefit someone I do not love, someone I do not like.' Getting angry without reason. Bhikkhus, these are the ten grounds for resentment.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.79
